title: Order Lifecycle Technical Reference
readerIntent: Trace contracts, state, owners, APIs, Pipelines, Workflows, events, security and verification.
owner: Order lifecycle implementation and contributing domain owners
summary: Reference for implementing, reviewing and testing cancellation, Return/RMA and Refund without parallel authority paths.

sections.heading: Aggregate and state
items: orderLifecycleRequest is the versioned intent aggregate; items preserve immutable order-entry scope and evidence references.
Common states include SUBMITTED, APPROVAL_PENDING, INFORMATION_REQUESTED, APPROVED or AUTHORIZED, EXECUTING, PARTIALLY_COMPLETED, COMPLETED, REJECTED and RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED.
Repository mutation uses request identity plus expected version. Duplicate business identity and stale revision are rejected or returned idempotently as defined by the operation.

sections.heading: Execution boundaries
items: Cancellation evaluation and calculation gather owner evidence before the execution Pipeline calls Fulfillment, Inventory, Payment and Product services.
Return Workflow creates Fulfillment RMAs; warehouse receipt and disposition Pipelines close them; an Order event listener derives final refund eligibility.
Refund calculation creates exact approved allocation evidence; Payment persists REQUESTED before the provider call and records normalized success or uncertain reconciliation state.

sections.heading: API and Axis
items: Customer and support intent endpoints are separately permissioned and scope ownership server-side.
Operations diagnostics and lifecycle policy management return bounded safe projections.
Authenticated bootstrap is the route authority. Workbench action metadata is filtered by permission and record state; Axis invokes the published backend operation with revision evidence.

sections.heading: Security invariants
items: Never accept caller-supplied owner evidence as authoritative where the backend can resolve it.
Never expose credentials, raw provider webhooks, document paths, unrestricted personal data or internal stack traces.
Validate callback signatures in the provider adapter before producing a normalized internal event. Enforce event replay protection and exact original-rail reconciliation.
Audit actor, source, correlation, state, reason, decision and evidence references; keep sensitive content outside audit messages.

sections.heading: Verification matrix
items: Cancellation: full, partial, pre-settlement, post-settlement, duplicate, owner failure and uncertain Payment.
Return: serialized, bulk, multi-RMA, partial receipt, invalid disposition, stale revision, inventory movement and replay.
Refund: full, partial, split payment, exact tax/shipping/discount, maker-checker, duplicate, timeout, verified callback and reconciliation.
Cross-capability: Notification outcome, KYC eligibility, permission filtering, customer override, generated context, structure, Axis, docs and environment topology.

sections.heading: Observability and production readiness
items: Correlate the lifecycle request, Workflow carrier, owner operation, provider transaction, audit entry and notification request without storing secrets or raw personal data.
Monitor queue age, approval SLA, execution latency, provider timeout, reconciliation backlog, duplicate rate, stale revision, notification failure and owner-specific exception counts.

Production readiness requires explicit provider account ownership, secret rotation, signed callback validation, bounded retries, circuit breaking, alert routing, operational runbooks, capacity evidence and tested recovery. A source adapter or deterministic fake is not proof of live qualification.
